contracts.native_title: An odd-period pedal-antipedal area invariant in elliptic billiards

contracts.native_title: An odd-period product for focal inversions of outer billiard polygons
contracts.native_Description: For a fixed odd least-period elliptic billiard family with a strictly nested nondegenerate confocal elliptical caustic, we prove constancy of the product of the signed straight-edge areas obtained by unit inversion of the outer tangent-polygon vertices about the two original billiard foci. Every admissible coprime star turning number, the critical triangular case and fixed repeated traversals are included. This proves the assertion conjectured as k904,a in Reznik--Garcia--Koiller arXiv2004.12497v11, Table10 (earlier v10 label k808,a). The proof gives the explicit inverse-edge factorization, cancels double principal parts in the cyclic area sum, and applies the classical complementary zero/pole divisor argument on a compact torus. Stachel canonical coordinates, established Jacobi and cyclic elliptic identities, and earlier complex billiard and complementary-area techniques are credited. Original-vertex inverse areas and outer-locus-focus inversions are distinct targets. No exact earlier general proof was verified in two independent bounded priority audits; historical novelty remains undetermined. The final journal text of The talented Mr. Inversive Triangle was subscription-limited, open author versions were read, and selected-passage and unresolved-source limitations are preserved. No first-proof, absolute-priority, new general elliptic-method or current-worldwide-open claim is made. The deposit includes a concise research note and a portable source/verification archive preserving original submissions, exact controls, separately labeled numerical diagnostics and authored audit records. contracts.original_abstract_TeX: For a periodic billiard family between an ellipse and a strictly nested nondegenerate confocal elliptical caustic, form the outer polygon by intersecting consecutive tangents at the billiard vertices. Invert its vertices in the unit circles centered at the two original billiard foci, and join successive images by straight segments. We prove that the product of the resulting signed areas is constant for every odd least period, including primitive stars. This proves the invariant conjectured as k904,a in the pinned 2020 list of Reznik, Garcia and Koiller. An explicit inverse-edge factorization reduces the area to a cyclic elliptic sum. Its double principal parts cancel, leaving two simple poles and complementary half-period zeros. The triangular critical case and repeated traversals are included. The analytic methods are classical; no first-proof or absolute-priority claim is made. This AI-assisted research note is unrefereed.

contracts.original_abstract_TeX:
We give an explicit affirmative answer to the two-polynomial question posed by
Austrin in Oberwolfach Report 9/2025. Two nonzero real multilinear polynomials
of degree at most \(d\) on the uniform Boolean cube have a common nonzero
vertex whenever every relative coordinate influence is at most
\(1/(4096d^8)\). In fact, disjoint supports force a relative influence at least
\(1/(1024d^8)\). The result is a deduction from the disjoint-support separator
of Li--Li--Li--Liu and the covariance inequality of
O'Donnell--Saks--Schramm--Servedio, combined with a square-density estimate.
We supply the complete deduction and an explicit separator constant.
No novelty or first-priority claim is made for this consequence.

contracts.native_title: Quantitative persistence in a fixed-city area equation
contracts.native_Description:
For every fixed finite collection of at least two distinct interior sites in the unit square and every strictly positive initial probability vector, consider the hard weighted-Voronoi area equation z_i prime = A_i(z) - z_i, where city i maximizes z_i^alpha times distance to the power -beta. We give a quantitative all-coordinate persistence theorem when beta > 2 alpha: an explicit time-dependent lower bound, a positive bound for all time, and a positive limiting inferior bound independent of the starting state. An asymmetric three-city instance with alpha=2, beta=8 has every share between 1/4096 and 2047/2048 for all nonnegative time. This refutes the unrestricted alpha > 1 collapse alternative in the literal 2007 Conjecture 32(a) and the catalog conjunction containing it. The result does not establish convergence, equilibrium uniqueness, initial-value independence of a limit, or stochastic city-founding conclusions. Zero initial weights, coincident sites, boundary sites, and the one-city case are outside the stated theorem.

The model and conjecture are Aldous's. Multiplicatively weighted Voronoi/Apollonius geometry is classical; the original 2007 notes already contain the protected-neighborhood mechanism and area exponent 2 alpha / beta in an unfinished stochastic argument. The scalar substitution and integrating-factor step are standard. Ferudun's unrefereed preprint, stated release 14 October 2026, explicitly gives robust two-city Conjecture 32(a) counterexamples in another parameter range and records the ratio-invariance inconsistency. Its proved every-exponent derivative lemma and position continuity also imply qualitative two-city noncollapse in the present beta > 2 alpha regime. These overlapping conclusions receive direct credit. The present theorem supplies all-site, all-positive-initial-state quantitative persistence; it is not advertised as the first negative answer or as a new geometric method. The original complete PR was recorded on 6 October 2026, but chronology and bounded searches certify neither firstness, exhaustive novelty nor worldwide current openness.

The deposit contains a five-page research note and a verification archive with editable source, all forty frozen original files, original nested evidence archives, independent analytical and bounded priority audit evidence, source version/hash locators, an externally pinned closed-inventory verifier and deterministic ZIP builder. Default finite replay runs the original witness/checker self-tests under normal and optimized Python. Optional full provenance requires three complete pinned corpora and two separately supplied primary PDFs. Primary publications, extracted source text, page images, raw dataset records and private credentials are excluded. Artifact hashes and finite checks do not certify the analytic theorem or priority. Compressed-byte reproducibility is limited to identical inputs and the same Python ZIP implementation and zlib runtime.

contracts.original_abstract_TeX: For finitely many fixed distinct interior sites in the unit square, let each site's positive population share grow at the rate of the area where its influence is maximal, minus its current share. Influence is proportional to population to the power $\alpha$ times distance to the power $-\beta$. We prove that every positive initial probability vector gives a global trajectory and, when $\beta>2\alpha$, every share has an explicit positive lower bound for all time. An asymmetric three-site instance with $\alpha=2$ and $\beta=8$ has all shares between $1/4096$ and $2047/2048$. This disproves the unrestricted $\alpha>1$ collapse alternative in the literal 2007 fixed-city conjecture. The result is a quantitative, all-site persistence statement; it does not establish convergence or resolve the stochastic city-founding model. We credit the original local geometric mechanism and a directly overlapping 2026 two-city counterexample analysis. No firstness claim is made.
